name: Landingi
summary: Landing page builder with 400+ templates and unlimited pages, capped by monthly visitors; A/B testing and pop-ups sit on a higher tier. Cheaper than Unbounce and Instapage, and the trade is no AI traffic routing, no real-time collaboration and thinner technical control.
best_for: budget-conscious teams, international businesses and anyone needing bulk or programmatic page generation across 29 languages
skip_if: you need AI traffic routing, real-time collaboration or deep technical control: that's where Unbounce earns its higher price
honest_knock: You trade away the high-end optimisation: no AI traffic routing like Unbounce's Smart Traffic, no real-time collaboration, and thinner technical control (script containers). Excellent value, but not the conversion-optimisation powerhouse.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-17, 2026-09-28 and 2026-11-28; the English page quotes USD while the same page served from a Dutch address quotes euros at the same numerals, so check your own currency) Four plans, billed annually: Build $24/month, Optimize $119/month, Scale from $229/month and Enterprise from $1,199/month. Annual billing includes two months free against monthly. Custom domains are metered: 1 on Build, 3 on Optimize, 10 on Scale and 100 on Enterprise, with extras at $5 a month each. AI credits come with the plan (2,500, 10,000, 20,000 and 60,000 a month) and top-ups are pay-as-you-go at $15 for 5,000, $25 for 10,000 and $40 for 20,000. A promotional rate roughly half the Build price appears periodically — it is a limited-time offer rather than the standard rate. On 28 November 2026 the page carried a banner reading 'Black Friday is ON! Up to 70% off Landingi' without per-plan sale prices; the FAQ amounts above were unchanged.

claims.claim: We have no designer, and every new offer waits weeks for someone to build its page.
claims.observed: A landing page was made from the Black Friday template, with the texts changed to made up text, and published on the test domain at 15:27, about 2 minutes and about 20 actions after the start at 15:26. No design work was needed.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: Our own clock times for one template against a dossier pain that gives no set-up time.
claims.buying_consequence: A first page can be online within a few minutes when you start from a template, but the time covers made up text and our own clock.

claims.observed: The welcome screen offered Generate page with AI (Lunar V. 1.5) or the Classic Drag & Drop Builder with templates. The goal Offer/Coupon download led to the Black Friday template, which already had a form and a thank-you page. The number of templates was not counted.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The welcome screen text against one template that was opened; no count of the library was made.
claims.buying_consequence: There is a template that comes with a form and a thank-you page, but the size of the library was not checked.

claims.observed: The English template showed Polish labels in its countdown timer. The spot is covered on screenshot 01. The dossier does not mention the language of template texts.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: Our own look at one template against a dossier that says nothing about template texts.
claims.buying_consequence: Read every text of a template in the language of your visitors before you publish it, because this English one carried Polish labels.

claims.claim: Your free trial ends in 14 days, and you have used 0 out of 200 unique visits.
claims.observed: The trial banner showed 14 days and 200 unique visits. After one test visit the counter read 1 out of 200, and Build lifts the limit to 2,000 unique visits.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The banner and the counter of the app against the dossier trial; the limit was not reached.
claims.buying_consequence: A live campaign can use up the 200 visits of the trial quickly; the dossier warning that the account may be blocked at the limit was not tested.

claims.claim: THANK YOU. Your discount code has been sent to the email you provided.
claims.observed: A test entry with an address at example.com showed this thank-you text. No mailbox was checked, so it is not known whether a discount mail was sent.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The thank-you text against a test that used an example address and no mailbox.
claims.buying_consequence: The form and the thank-you page work, but whether the mail with the code arrives was not seen.

claims.observed: The entry showed up in Leads at once with the origin Sample Snowboards - Winter... and 18 Nov 2026 03:28 PM, and the page list read 1 visit and 1 lead.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The Leads page and the page list against the one entry that was made.
claims.buying_consequence: Leads from the form are stored in the dashboard right away, so you do not need another tool to see them.

claims.claim: Build 24 EUR/month billed annually (SAVE 60 EUR), 2,000 visits, 10 published landing pages, 1 custom domain
claims.observed: Build billed annually costs 24 EUR a month and gives 2,000 visits a month, 10 published landing pages and 1 custom domain, as in the dossier (10 active pages, 2,000 visits, 1 domain). The amount is in euros, the dossier names dollars with the same number.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The Build plan card in euros against the dossier Build plan; the same number, a different currency.
claims.buying_consequence: Build covers a few offers with modest traffic; check the currency on your own checkout.

claims.claim: plus Smart Sections, A/B Testing, E-Commerce Hub, Popups
claims.observed: On the plan screen Smart Sections and A/B Testing are listed under Optimize and not under Build, at 109 EUR a month billed annually. A/B testing was not used.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The plan screen against the dossier line that A/B testing starts on Optimize; the feature itself was not used.
claims.buying_consequence: To test two versions of a page you need Optimize and not the cheap Build plan.

claims.observed: Billed annually Optimize is 109 EUR a month, Scale 209 EUR and Enterprise 1,050 EUR in the app and on the public page for a Dutch address. The dossier lists 119, 229 and 1,199 (in dollars) and says the same numbers appear in euros.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The euro prices of the app against the dossier dollar prices; the dollar view could not be opened.
claims.buying_consequence: In euros the higher plans cost less than the dossier numbers; check which currency and price you get at your own checkout.

claims.observed: Billed monthly Optimize is 139 EUR with a FIRST-MONTH OFFER of 29 EUR (save 110 EUR), while Build is 29, Scale 269 and Enterprise 1,350 EUR. The price after the first month was not tested.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The monthly view of the plan screen against a dossier that names a promotional rate only for the entry plan.
claims.buying_consequence: The first month of Optimize is cheap, but plan for 139 EUR a month afterwards.

claims.claim: You can cancel your subscription at any time. It takes just a few clicks in your account settings.
claims.observed: No paid plan was started, so no cancel step was seen. Under Settings, My profile there is Delete account, which removes the account with all its content; it was not confirmed.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The cancel text of the checkout against a test that started no paid plan.
claims.buying_consequence: The way out of a paid plan was not seen; deleting the account removes everything.

claims.observed: Build billed annually opened a summary of 288 EUR a year (24 EUR x 12 months) with Total now 288 EUR and a 30-day Money Back Guarantee. The payment screen kept Pay now greyed out, nothing was filled in and no VAT line was shown before the billing details.
claims.plan: Free 14 day trial with 200 unique visits; the Build plan billed annually was opened up to the empty payment screen, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The plan page price against the summary total; no VAT, fee or stored cost rule could be compared before the billing details.
claims.buying_consequence: A year of Build is 288 EUR, and VAT may come on top once you fill in your company details.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session made a landing page from the Black Friday template in Landingi under the free 14 day trial, changed the texts and published it on the test domain of Landingi in about 2 minutes and about 20 actions, without a card. The English template showed Polish labels in its countdown timer. One test form entry gave a thank-you page and showed up in Leads at once (1 visit, 1 lead). The trial allows 200 unique visits; Build allows 2,000 visits a month, 10 published pages and 1 domain. In euros the yearly prices were Build 24, Optimize 109, Scale 209 and Enterprise 1,050 a month, monthly 29, 139, 269 and 1,350, with a first-month offer of 29 on Optimize; the dossier lists dollar prices (24, 119, 229 and 1,199), so only Build is the same. Build billed annually came to 288 EUR for a year with no VAT line before the billing details. Nothing was paid, the test page was unpublished again and the account was not deleted. Account and start: the account was created by us and was signed in in his Chrome (the interface was in English); our AI assistant ran the test from 15:26 (Amsterdam). The dossier name is Landingi and the review is on MSS (mss/landingi-review.html). The audience tested from the dossier: Small teams publishing a few landing pages (We have no designer, and every new offer waits weeks for someone to build its page.). The groups Marketers who want to A/B test pages and Paid-traffic agencies wanting AI page routing were not tested. Start: the welcome screen asked How do you want to build your first landing page? with Generate page with AI (Lunar V. 1.5) or Classic Drag & Drop Builder (choose from 400+ fully customizable templates). The trial banner read Your free trial ends in 14 days, and you have used 0 out of 200 unique visits, and says that Build lifts the limit to 2,000 unique visits. Core action: Build page, Pick a template, the goal Offer/Coupon download, the template Black Friday, the name Sample Snowboards - Winter Wax Kit, then the editor. The heading (WINTER WAX OFFER), the body text and the offer title (Winter Wax Kit) were changed to made up text. The template already has a form (email, Choose your discount, a tick I agree to receive promotional emails and offers from this store., the button SEND) and a thank-you page. Publish: the window Follow the tips to refine page performance (SEO, favicon, thumbnail) offered Publish anyway; the page went live on the test domain of Landingi at 15:27 (opened 15:27:54), so about 2 minutes and about 20 actions from the start. Publishing Options says The test domain is set as the MAIN URL. Finding: the English template showed Polish labels in the countdown timer (the words for days, hours, minutes and seconds); that spot is covered on screenshot 01. Form entry: a test entry with an address at example.com, the choice Shoes 50%off, the tick on and SEND gave the thank-you page THANK YOU. Your discount code has been sent to the email you provided. The Leads page showed one row with that address, the origin Sample Snowboards - Winter... and 18 Nov 2026 03:28 PM; the page list showed Visits 1 and Leads 1 (100%); the trial counter read 1 out of 200 unique visits. Whether a discount mail really arrived was not checked. Plans: Choose your plan (Buy now in the trial banner), read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 with a Dutch account, in EUR. Billed annually, per month: Build 24 EUR (save 60 EUR), Optimize 109 EUR (save 360 EUR), Scale 209 EUR (save 720 EUR) and Enterprise 1,050 EUR (save 3,600 EUR). Billed monthly: Build 29 EUR, Optimize 139 EUR with a FIRST-MONTH OFFER of 29 EUR (save 110 EUR), Scale 269 EUR and Enterprise 1,350 EUR. Limits: Build 2,000 visits a month, 10 published landing pages, 1 custom domain, 5 users and 2,500 credits; Optimize 30,000 visits, 100 pages, 3 domains, 10 users and 10,000 credits, plus Smart Sections, A/B Testing, E-Commerce Hub, Popups, Multi-lang Personalization, Global JavaScript snippets, Webhook and Funnels; Scale 100,000 visits (a list to pick more), unlimited pages, 10 domains and 20,000 credits; Enterprise from 1,000,000 visits and 100 domains. The trial gives 14 days and 200 unique visits. Configuration for Build billed annually: 288 EUR a year (24 EUR x 12 months), Total now 288 EUR, You can cancel your subscription at any time and a 30-day Money Back Guarantee. The payment screen (Company or Individual, Country Netherlands, company name, EU VAT number, address, Credit card or PayPal) kept Pay now greyed out; nothing was filled in and no VAT line was shown before the billing details were entered. The public page landingi.com/pricing was read again just before this delivery the same day from a Dutch address: it showed euros as well, with the same amounts (yearly view Build 24, Optimize 109, Scale 209 and Enterprise 1,050; monthly view Build 29, Optimize 139 with a first-month discount of 29, Scale 269 and Enterprise 1,350). A dollar view could not be opened from here, so the dossier prices in USD (24, 119, 229 and 1,199 a month billed annually) could not be checked in dollars. Deviation: in euros the Optimize, Scale and Enterprise prices are lower than the dossier numerals (109 against 119, 209 against 229, 1,050 against 1,199), while the dossier says the same numerals appear in euros; only Build is the same (24). Verify the dollar prices on the live page before publication. Cancelling: no subscription was started (trial). Settings (the gear at the bottom left), My profile has Delete account: You will permanently delete your account with all its content. It was not confirmed. A paid plan is cancelled, according to the app, in your account settings. Not tested: A/B testing, EventTracker, Smart Sections, AI routing, a custom domain, WordPress, integrations, paying, cancelling a subscription and the mobile view. Clean up: the test page Sample Snowboards - Winter Wax Kit was unpublished again (the message Your page is set as unpublished) and the test page and the test lead stay in the account; the account was not deleted and nothing was paid; one browser tab was used and closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The English template had Polish labels in its countdown timer, so check every text of a template before you publish it. The trial stops at 200 unique visits and Build at 2,000 visits a month, so a real campaign can use that up. A/B testing, Smart Sections and the E-Commerce Hub start on Optimize, not on Build. The first month of Optimize is cheaper in the monthly view, so look at the price of the month after it. The VAT line is only shown after you fill in the billing details. Deleting the account removes all its content.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.

not_tested: A/B testing, EventTracker, Smart Sections and AI routing.
A custom domain, WordPress and integrations, and the mobile view.
Paying, the VAT line after the billing details, and cancelling a paid plan; the account was not deleted.
Whether the discount mail of the thank-you page really arrived.
Export of a file into a kit, and reimport.

Session and source-reading date: 18 November 2026. Times are CET. The session started at about 15:26 CET. These are approximate tester observations, not benchmark timings. Midnight timestamps are required date anchors, not measured event times.
exit_test.note: A check of this export route with synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Re-importing the export was not tested. The exported file was not opened, so what it contains is unverified. Friction is described, not scored; this is not a verdict on the product.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session made a landing page from the Black Friday template in Landingi under the free 14 day trial, changed the texts and published it on the test domain of Landingi in about 2 minutes and about 20 actions, without a card. The English template showed Polish labels in its countdown timer. One test form entry gave a thank-you page and showed up in Leads at once (1 visit, 1 lead). The trial allows 200 unique visits; Build allows 2,000 visits a month, 10 published pages and 1 domain. In euros the yearly prices were Build 24, Optimize 109, Scale 209 and Enterprise 1,050 a month, monthly 29, 139, 269 and 1,350, with a first-month offer of 29 on Optimize; the dossier lists dollar prices (24, 119, 229 and 1,199), so only Build is the same. Build billed annually came to 288 EUR for a year with no VAT line before the billing details. Nothing was paid, the test page was unpublished again and the account was not deleted.
findings: Text we checked: "Your free trial ends in 14 days, and you have used 0 out of 200 unique visits". What we saw: The trial banner showed 14 days and 200 unique visits. After one test visit the counter read 1 out of 200, and Build lifts the limit to 2,000 unique visits.

Text we checked: "Visits 1, Leads 1 (100%)". What we saw: The entry showed up in Leads at once with the origin Sample Snowboards - Winter... and 18 Nov 2026 03:28 PM, and the page list read 1 visit and 1 lead.

Text we checked: "Build 24 EUR/month billed annually (SAVE 60 EUR), 2,000 visits, 10 published landing pages, 1 custom domain". What we saw: Build billed annually costs 24 EUR a month and gives 2,000 visits a month, 10 published landing pages and 1 custom domain, as in the dossier (10 active pages, 2,000 visits, 1 domain). The amount is in euros, the dossier names dollars with the same number.

Text we checked: "plus Smart Sections, A/B Testing, E-Commerce Hub, Popups". What we saw: On the plan screen Smart Sections and A/B Testing are listed under Optimize and not under Build, at 109 EUR a month billed annually. A/B testing was not used.

Text we checked: "Optimize 109 EUR (SAVE 360)". What we saw: Billed annually Optimize is 109 EUR a month, Scale 209 EUR and Enterprise 1,050 EUR in the app and on the public page for a Dutch address. The dossier lists 119, 229 and 1,199 (in dollars) and says the same numbers appear in euros.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session made a landing page from the Black Friday template in Landingi under the free 14 day trial, changed the texts and published it on the test domain of Landingi in about 2 minutes and about 20 actions, without a card. The English template showed Polish labels in its countdown timer. One test form entry gave a thank-you page and showed up in Leads at once (1 visit, 1 lead). The trial allows 200 unique visits; Build allows 2,000 visits a month, 10 published pages and 1 domain. In euros the yearly prices were Build 24, Optimize 109, Scale 209 and Enterprise 1,050 a month, monthly 29, 139, 269 and 1,350, with a first-month offer of 29 on Optimize; the dossier lists dollar prices (24, 119, 229 and 1,199), so only Build is the same. Build billed annually came to 288 EUR for a year with no VAT line before the billing details. Nothing was paid, the test page was unpublished again and the account was not deleted. Account and start: the account was created by us and was signed in in his Chrome (the interface was in English); our AI assistant ran the test from 15:26 (Amsterdam). The dossier name is Landingi and the review is on MSS (mss/landingi-review.html). The audience tested from the dossier: Small teams publishing a few landing pages (We have no designer, and every new offer waits weeks for someone to build its page.). The groups Marketers who want to A/B test pages and Paid-traffic agencies wanting AI page routing were not tested. Start: the welcome screen asked How do you want to build your first landing page? with Generate page with AI (Lunar V. 1.5) or Classic Drag & Drop Builder (choose from 400+ fully customizable templates). The trial banner read Your free trial ends in 14 days, and you have used 0 out of 200 unique visits, and says that Build lifts the limit to 2,000 unique visits. Core action: Build page, Pick a template, the goal Offer/Coupon download, the template Black Friday, the name Sample Snowboards - Winter Wax Kit, then the editor. The heading (WINTER WAX OFFER), the body text and the offer title (Winter Wax Kit) were changed to made up text. The template already has a form (email, Choose your discount, a tick I agree to receive promotional emails and offers from this store., the button SEND) and a thank-you page. Publish: the window Follow the tips to refine page performance (SEO, favicon, thumbnail) offered Publish anyway; the page went live on the test domain of Landingi at 15:27 (opened 15:27:54), so about 2 minutes and about 20 actions from the start. Publishing Options says The test domain is set as the MAIN URL. Finding: the English template showed Polish labels in the countdown timer (the words for days, hours, minutes and seconds); that spot is covered on screenshot 01. Form entry: a test entry with an address at example.com, the choice Shoes 50%off, the tick on and SEND gave the thank-you page THANK YOU. Your discount code has been sent to the email you provided. The Leads page showed one row with that address, the origin Sample Snowboards - Winter... and 18 Nov 2026 03:28 PM; the page list showed Visits 1 and Leads 1 (100%); the trial counter read 1 out of 200 unique visits. Whether a discount mail really arrived was not checked. Plans: Choose your plan (Buy now in the trial banner), read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 with a Dutch account, in EUR. Billed annually, per month: Build 24 EUR (save 60 EUR), Optimize 109 EUR (save 360 EUR), Scale 209 EUR (save 720 EUR) and Enterprise 1,050 EUR (save 3,600 EUR). Billed monthly: Build 29 EUR, Optimize 139 EUR with a FIRST-MONTH OFFER of 29 EUR (save 110 EUR), Scale 269 EUR and Enterprise 1,350 EUR. Limits: Build 2,000 visits a month, 10 published landing pages, 1 custom domain, 5 users and 2,500 credits; Optimize 30,000 visits, 100 pages, 3 domains, 10 users and 10,000 credits, plus Smart Sections, A/B Testing, E-Commerce Hub, Popups, Multi-lang Personalization, Global JavaScript snippets, Webhook and Funnels; Scale 100,000 visits (a list to pick more), unlimited pages, 10 domains and 20,000 credits; Enterprise from 1,000,000 visits and 100 domains. The trial gives 14 days and 200 unique visits. Configuration for Build billed annually: 288 EUR a year (24 EUR x 12 months), Total now 288 EUR, You can cancel your subscription at any time and a 30-day Money Back Guarantee. The payment screen (Company or Individual, Country Netherlands, company name, EU VAT number, address, Credit card or PayPal) kept Pay now greyed out; nothing was filled in and no VAT line was shown before the billing details were entered. The public page landingi.com/pricing was read again just before this delivery the same day from a Dutch address: it showed euros as well, with the same amounts (yearly view Build 24, Optimize 109, Scale 209 and Enterprise 1,050; monthly view Build 29, Optimize 139 with a first-month discount of 29, Scale 269 and Enterprise 1,350). A dollar view could not be opened from here, so the dossier prices in USD (24, 119, 229 and 1,199 a month billed annually) could not be checked in dollars. Deviation: in euros the Optimize, Scale and Enterprise prices are lower than the dossier numerals (109 against 119, 209 against 229, 1,050 against 1,199), while the dossier says the same numerals appear in euros; only Build is the same (24). Verify the dollar prices on the live page before publication. Cancelling: no subscription was started (trial). Settings (the gear at the bottom left), My profile has Delete account: You will permanently delete your account with all its content. It was not confirmed. A paid plan is cancelled, according to the app, in your account settings. Not tested: A/B testing, EventTracker, Smart Sections, AI routing, a custom domain, WordPress, integrations, paying, cancelling a subscription and the mobile view. Clean up: the test page Sample Snowboards - Winter Wax Kit was unpublished again (the message Your page is set as unpublished) and the test page and the test lead stay in the account; the account was not deleted and nothing was paid; one browser tab was used and closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The English template had Polish labels in its countdown timer, so check every text of a template before you publish it. The trial stops at 200 unique visits and Build at 2,000 visits a month, so a real campaign can use that up. A/B testing, Smart Sections and the E-Commerce Hub start on Optimize, not on Build. The first month of Optimize is cheaper in the monthly view, so look at the price of the month after it. The VAT line is only shown after you fill in the billing details. Deleting the account removes all its content.
